Four tools could not answer at all. They can now. Every response in the server also
got smaller along the way. No tool was added or removed — the server still declares
109.

## Four tools were too large to return

`get_available_badges`, `get_sleep_data`, `get_earned_badges` and `get_stress_data`
each handed back the Garmin payload exactly as it arrived. For all four that ran past
the limit on how much a single tool result may carry, so the answer never reached the
model: asking about last night's sleep produced an error, not a short night.

This was not slowness or expense. The tools were unusable.

| Tool | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `get_available_badges` | ~85,000 tokens | ~15,000 |
| `get_sleep_data` | ~44,000 tokens | ~1,400 |
| `get_earned_badges` | ~41,000 tokens | ~10,000 |
| `get_stress_data` | ~28,000 tokens | ~100 |

Nothing that used to be reachable has been taken away. Each of these tools now
answers with the summary that the question usually wants, and keeps the full payload
behind a flag — the same bargain `get_floors` struck in v4.4.0:

```
get_sleep_data(date: "2026-08-22", includeTimeSeries: true)
get_stress_data(date: "2026-08-22", includeValues: true)
get_earned_badges(includeDetails: true)
```

`get_sleep_data` is the clearest case. A night carries six parallel per-minute series
— movement alone is around 640 points — and every one of them already has a tool of
its own: `get_sleep_movement`, `get_hrv_data`, `get_respiration_data`. It now returns
the nightly summary, the sleep stages and the scores, then names each series it left
out and how many points it holds, so it is obvious what to ask for next.

## Every response got smaller

Tool results were being pretty-printed with two-space indentation. Indentation is for
people reading files, and nobody reads these: they go straight into a model's context,
where each space costs the same as a letter.

Printing them compactly cut about 58% from every response across all 109 tools, not
only the four above. Nothing about the data changed — only the whitespace between it.

## `get_stress_data` reports durations again

It was meant to tell you how long the day was spent resting, low, medium and high. It
read those figures straight off the `dailyStress` response, which does not send them,
so they were quietly absent from every answer it ever gave. The old `raw` field —
which repeated every value already listed above it — made this hard to spot.

The endpoint does send the samples, so the four durations are now worked out from
those. No extra request, and the tool finally reports what it always said it would.

## Verified

Every read-only tool — 66 of them — was run against a live Garmin account after the
change. All answered, none errored, none exceeded the limit.

## Install

Download `garmin-mcp-ts.mcpb` and open it with Claude Desktop, or drag it onto
Settings → Extensions. Verify the download first:

```
sha256sum -c garmin-mcp-ts.mcpb.sha256
```

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/sedoglia/garmin-mcp-ts/compare/v4.4.0...v4.5.0
